label: sec:qbeta-per-block-delta-tau-intro
html:
The previous section evaluated the Markov trace block by block. We now read these characters through the T_\beta endomorphism.

The per-block characters \chi_\lambda(\Delta_{T_\beta})(q) over H_3(q) admit closed forms and vanish at the classical point q = 1 (prop:qbeta-per-block-chi-closed-forms). Once the Markov weights take their canonical values, this vanishing forces the trace difference \Delta\mathrm{tr}_M to carry an explicit (q^2-1) factor (prop:qbeta-delta-tau-canonical-conditional-q2-minus-1-factor). We formalise this conditional statement via a class hypothesis, which we inhabit with an explicit \sqrt{q}-bearing instance (prop:qbeta-canonical-markov-weights-explicit-instance).

The low-order Taylor data of the surrogate \Delta\mathrm{tr}_M (prop:qbeta-delta-tau-surrogate-taylor-coefficients) provides the exact per-block input required by the downstream decay-side c_k recursion. In contrast, the downstream extraction itself relies on calibration anchoring.
